name: Kiro Dhow
description: A full-stack rental platform that replaces paper receipts and scattered chats with role-based dashboards, live landlord–tenant messaging, map-based property search, and automated rent billing.
overview: Kiro Dhow digitizes the entire residential leasing lifecycle into a single web application. Replacing fragmented communication, paper receipts, and manual tracking, the platform delivers isolated portals for tenants, landlords, and system administrators—handling everything from map-based property search to automated lease billing and real-time maintenance dispatching.
features: Multi-tenant RBAC architecture with isolated dashboards and JWT auth for Tenants, Landlords, and Admins
Real-time bidirectional landlord-tenant messaging powered by Socket.io with unread indicators
Interactive property search engine integrated with Leaflet maps and Material-UI filtering
End-to-end lease lifecycle management featuring automated rent billing via Node-cron background jobs
Centralized maintenance ticketing system with Multer file uploads and resolution state tracking
Financial and occupancy reporting suite visualised with Chart.js
challenges: The hardest part was keeping one codebase honest across two databases — SQLite in development, MySQL in production — so every schema change went through Knex.js migrations to stop drift before it started. Keeping WebSocket events and Redux state in sync took the same care, so the UI never showed a stale number.

name: University of Hargeisa Hackathon — 1st Place
description: A university ride-sharing platform — React Native app, React admin dashboard, and an Express API — designed, built, and shipped in 48 hours to take 1st place out of 8 teams.
overview: Led a cross-functional team to design, build, and ship a full-stack ride-sharing platform for the University of Hargeisa student body in a 48-hour sprint: a React Native mobile app for students and drivers, a React-based admin dashboard, and an Express.js REST API tying it together. The submission won 1st place out of 8 competing teams.
features: Ride booking, driver assignment, and route/schedule management
Real-time notifications and booking cancellation over Socket.io
Secure REST APIs with JWT authentication and role-based access control
Relational database schema supporting operational reporting and analytics
challenges: The constraint was time, not scope — with 48 hours on the clock and three surfaces to build (mobile app, admin dashboard, API), the real work was scoping ruthlessly as team lead so every piece shipped working end-to-end instead of one polished feature surrounded by half-finished ones.

name: Caraabe
description: A regional bus booking system: riders pick seats on an interactive map and pay with Zaad mobile money, while admins run routes, fleets, and payment checks from a single panel.
overview: Caraabe digitizes regional bus operations by replacing manual processes with real-time seat tracking and mobile payments. Built with native PHP and MySQL, it features dynamic 2+aisle+2 bus seat selection, automated Zaad USSD payment workflows, round-trip discount linking, and QR code ticket generation.
features: Interactive seat selection (2+aisle+2 layout) with driver seat reservation protection
Integrated Zaad mobile money payment workflow with USSD code generator and admin verification
Round-trip booking engine using 4-digit linked discount codes
Dynamic digital tickets featuring QR codes and active status tracking
Admin suite for bus fleet management, weekly recurring schedules, and route occupancy reporting
challenges: With no ORM to lean on, seat locking was raw PHP and MySQL: two riders hitting the same seat in the same second couldn't both win it, and the recurring weekly schedules had to generate cleanly without ever double-booking a seat.

name: E-Fiiri
description: A football league manager that publishes standings, fixtures, and rosters online — and recalculates the table automatically from every match result.
overview: E-Fiiri gives local football leagues a simple way to publish standings, fixtures, and player rosters online, instead of updating a printed table after every matchday.
features: Automatically calculated league standings from match results
Team and player profile pages
Fixture scheduling with upcoming and past matches
Live score updates during matchdays
challenges: Getting the standings table to recalculate correctly (points, goal difference, head-to-head) directly from raw match results in SQL took a few iterations to get right.

name: IEditor
description: A browser-based code playground for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with an instant live preview — no setup, no build step, everything runs client-side.
overview: IEditor is a lightweight, in-browser code playground for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. I built it to have a fast, no-setup place to prototype UI ideas, similar to CodePen, with an instant live preview pane.
features: Three-pane editor for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Live preview that updates as you type
Syntax-friendly editor panes with resizable layout
Runs entirely client-side, no build step required
challenges: Rendering the live preview safely and efficiently on every keystroke, without a heavy framework, meant writing a small debounce layer and injecting the combined output into a sandboxed iframe.
